bpm.short: The number of heartbeats in one minute. A normal resting heart rate for adults is 60–100 bpm.

mmHg.short: The standard unit for measuring blood pressure. A healthy baseline is around 120/80 mmHg.

mg/dL.short: A unit measuring blood sugar (glucose) concentration. Normal fasting levels are typically 70–99 mg/dL.

ECG.short: A recording of the heart's electrical activity used to check heart rate and rhythm.

cardiovascular.short: The heart and blood vessels working together to deliver oxygen and nutrients throughout the body.

sphygmomanometer.short: A medical blood pressure cuff and gauge used to measure arterial blood pressure.

systolic.short: The pressure in your arteries when the heart contracts and pumps blood out.

diastolic.short: The pressure in your arteries when the heart rests between beats.

thermoregulation.short: The body's ability to keep its core temperature stable (~36.6 °C) despite external temperature changes.

hypothermia.short: A dangerous drop in core body temperature below 35.0 °C when the body loses heat faster than it produces it.

glucose.short: The main sugar in your blood and primary energy source for your brain and muscles.

insulin.short: A hormone that helps glucose move from the bloodstream into cells to be used for energy.

hypoglycemia.short: A condition where blood glucose falls below 70 mg/dL, which can cause dizziness, weakness, or confusion.

circadian.short: The body's internal ~24-hour biological clock that regulates sleep, alertness, and hormone cycles.

microgravity.short: Near-weightlessness in orbit, causing body fluids to shift upward toward the head and chest.
